title: Database Security: Role Inheritance, Schema search_path Poisoning, and SECURITY DEFINER
realWorldScenario: A database security review reveals a function `process_refund(order_id INT)` created with `SECURITY DEFINER` by a `postgres` superuser. A junior engineer added an unprivileged tenant user who was able to execute arbitrary code with superuser privileges.
questionStatement: Explain the security risks of `SECURITY DEFINER` functions in PostgreSQL. What is `search_path` hijacking/poisoning, how do attackers exploit it, and what are the mandatory defensive measures (including `SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp`) required when creating privileged functions?
expectedConcepts: SECURITY DEFINER executing as function owner (setuid analogy)
search_path resolution order and object substitution attack
Exploitation via public schema or pg_temp shadow functions
Mandatory SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp clause
Explicit schema qualification (public.table) and REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC
hints: What happens if a caller has search_path = "malicious_schema, public"?
What does SET search_path = pg_catalog do inside the function definition?
Who can execute a newly created function by default in PostgreSQL?
